A1.justification: Both PDFs describe RoboSpatial and contain complete, readable main text and Appendices A–D. Corresponding methods, tables, equations, and figures can be reliably matched, including Figure 1 through visual inspection.

before.justification: Section 4 and Appendix D report original VLM evaluations, robot experiments, data-scaling results, and grounding ablations.

after.justification: Section 4 and Appendix D retain original experiments, including revised RoboSpatial-Home results in Table 4 and robot and ablation results in Tables 6 and 11.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same geometric annotation pipeline, three reference frames, spatial context and compatibility procedures, and auxiliary grounding supervision. Model fine-tuning and robot execution procedures are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same five source datasets, spatial tasks, RoboSpatial-Val/Home, BLINK, SpatialBench, and robot scenarios. Appendix evaluations on MMMU, MME, and MMBench are also retained.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged within corresponding experiments. Tables 3–4 retain the same eight VLM families and fine-tuned variants; Table 6 retains LLaVA-NeXT, RoboPoint, Molmo, and GPT-4o.

E3.justification: The stated splits, metrics, model configurations, training budgets, 6,000 validation questions, and 350 Home questions remain unchanged. No reported protocol revision accompanies the Table 4 score replacements.

E4.justification: Cross-dataset transfer, reference-frame analysis, annotation scaling, knowledge retention, and grounding ablations remain in Tables 5 and 8–11. The qualitative comparisons and robot failure examples in Figures 3–4 and 6–7 are also unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. Single-score reporting remains unchanged, including for the revised Table 4 entries.

E6.justification: Table 4 substantially revises RoboSpatial-Home results: 18 scores change across LLaVA-NeXT, SpaceLLaVA, RoboPoint, Molmo, and GPT-4o. RoboPoint's base/fine-tuned context scores change from 2.5/21.3 to 19.7/31.1, while its fine-tuned compatibility score changes from 88.6 to 81.0. These replacements materially alter comparison margins. BLINK, SpatialBench, and the other results tables remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Section 3.2 retains the same mathematical definitions of dataset entries, spatial relations, and reference frames. No substantive mathematical reasoning, assumptions, proofs, or derivations are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about dataset scale, spatial and reference-frame coverage, improved VLM reasoning, generalization, and robot applicability. Revised scores do not change the stated contributions.

C2.justification: Interpretations of linguistic transfer, grounding failures, and 2D/3D pretraining confounds remain unchanged. Appendix limitations concerning occupancy maps, containment, dataset coverage, and stacked objects are retained; Table 4 revisions receive no new interpretation.

D1.justification: Appendices B–D retain the same annotation counts, checkpoints, training instructions, eight-H100 setup, 20–40-hour training times, and robot implementation details. Stated code and data access information is unchanged.

R1.justification: v5 adds Zhang et al., 'Do vision-language models represent space and how? evaluating spatial frame of reference under ambiguities,' as reference 65 supporting the introduction's existing spatial-understanding critique. The research positioning otherwise remains unchanged; subsequent references are merely renumbered.

P1.justification: Limited copyediting includes changing 'robotics manipulation' to 'robot manipulation' in the abstract. Nearly all prose and the organization of Sections 1–5 and Appendices A–D remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 1 changes marker colors and label styling while retaining the same scenes, questions, and answers. Table 9 removes the 'Annotation Size' header and adjusts header formatting. Minor text reflow occurs without substantive figure or table reorganization.

improvement.justification: The added citation and small presentation edits provide limited benefits. However, the main substantive revision replaces many Table 4 scores without explaining their provenance or changing the stated settings. The PDFs do not establish whether these replacements improve result reliability, so the overall quality direction remains uncertain.
